entries.effect: the gamma and beta gradients are the header's formulas, they are measured beside a hand-computed reference in the case file, and both cases are bit-identical to the release. The data gradient is the full backpropagation gamma/sqrt(variance+epsilon) * (dY - mean(dY) - yhat/n * sum(dY)), which is the form the forward's own definition implies, and the release's value is not that expression: 11 of its 12 elements differ, the largest relative distance is 1.4, and this port's value over the release's runs from 0.399 to 11.6. MPSMatrixBatchNormalization.h documents the forward only, so the release's backward is not derivable from it. That case is named as owed in tests/backports/host/mpsmatrix/owed.tsv.

entries.effect: the product of the two matrices with the interior columns the descriptor names and the alpha and beta the caller sets, accumulated in double and written as float32; batchStart and batchSize bound the batch the release writes. The multiply, half-multiply and vector cases are bit-identical. The one that differs is multiply-batch, where the release ignores batchStart and writes the matrices of the whole range while the port writes only the range the header names, so four of its twelve elements are 1, 2, 3, 4 against 0. The port follows the header; that case is named as owed in tests/backports/host/mpsmatrix/owed.tsv, with the six-row table in facts/MetalPerformanceShaders/Matrix.md.

entries.effect: every neuron type of MPSCNNNeuronType.h is evaluated from that header's own formula on the CPU, in double, on the caller's alpha and bias. The family's largest distance is 800 units in the last place and 7.02e-05 relative, and it is GeLU, type 15, on element 8 of that case: the release's kernel is not the header's exact erf form. Every other differing element of the family is within 2 units. That case is named as owed in tests/backports/host/mpsmatrix/owed.tsv, and tests/backports/host/mpsmatrix/rank.py prints that family's row of the per-family table on every run.
